title: How writers use language and show their views

steps.say: Writers choose words to make readers feel or picture something.
steps.show: The storm roared.     The storm was loud.

steps.say: Ask: what does this word or phrase make me imagine or feel?
A writer’s purpose is the reason for writing: to inform, to persuade, to explain or to entertain.
A writer’s viewpoint is what they think. Look for opinion words such as I believe, sadly and terrible.
When you compare two texts, look at what is the same and what is different.

check.prompt: Read: Sadly, the old cinema will close forever next week. What does the word sadly show?

options.text: The writer is unhappy that the cinema will close.

options.why: Sadly is about the writer’s feeling, not the films.
Old tells us its age, but sadly shows a feeling.

hints: It tells us how the writer feels about the news.
Ask: is the writer happy or unhappy about the cinema closing?
check.explanation: Sadly shows the writer’s viewpoint: they are unhappy that the cinema will close.

check.prompt: What is the main purpose of an advert for a new water park?

options.why: That is the purpose of a story.

options.text: to give instructions for building a park
options.why: That is the purpose of instructions.
That is the purpose of a diary.

hints: Think about why adverts are made.
An advert wants the reader to do something.
Ask: what does the water park want you to do?
check.explanation: Adverts are written to persuade. An advert for a water park wants people to visit.
